title: Placeholder Typed Spawn
why: Barrel/enemy/powerup spawning is quota-based (stageBudgets per type) but the user wants the macro placeholder to be the source of truth: each placement declares 'random' or a specific type id from its family registry, and the composer spawns exactly that. Quotas are deleted.
outcomes: Deterministic typed spawn from macro data / dynamic type lists from object registries (no hardcoded editor values) / macro editor click-cycles random->types / all existing macros migrated to random / quota machinery removed

milestones.name: Object Type Registries
milestones.objective: Each object family (barrel, enemy, powerup) exposes an ordered [{id,label}] list + lookup helpers so editor and composer derive type options dynamically.
milestones.success: BARREL_TYPES, ENEMY_TYPES({id,label}), POWERUP_ROLL_TYPES all importable without circular-import TDZ; labels available for UI.
milestones.diagram:
graph LR
  A[object.js BARREL_TYPES] --> C[composer]
  B[build.js ENEMY_TYPES] --> C
  D[powerup.js POWERUP_ROLL_TYPES] --> C
  A --> E[macro editor]
  B --> E
  D --> E

tasks.name: Barrel registry
tasks.what: Add BARREL_TYPES ordered [{id,label}] list plus barrelById/isBarrelType to objects/object.js. Ids match BARREL_FACTORIES keys in world/build.js (wood/explosive/coin).
tasks.why: Barrels have no factory list today; the editor and schema need a dynamic source of barrel types.
acceptance: importing object.js standalone succeeds (no TDZ)
BARREL_TYPES has exactly wood/explosive/coin with labels

tasks.name: Enemy registry with labels
tasks.what: Rework ENEMY_FACTORIES in world/build.js so each entry carries a display label; export ENEMY_TYPES as ordered [{id,label}] plus enemyById/isEnemyType and ENEMY_TYPE_IDS for enum pickers. stats.js keeps its local ENEMY_KEYS (no import from build.js — circular).
tasks.why: Enemies already have a factory map but no labels; the editor tooltip/cycle needs them, and stats must not create an import cycle.
acceptance: importing build.js standalone succeeds
makeEnemy still works via f.make(x,y)
stats.js loads without importing build.js

tasks.name: Placement value validation
tasks.what: Add optional 'value' to validatePlacement in world/macroSchema.js: non-empty string; if not 'random' it must be a valid id for the placement's family (barrel/enemy/powerup registries). Document it in macros/macro.schema.json.
tasks.why: The composer will spawn exactly what the placeholder declares, so invalid data must fail at load time, never default silently.
acceptance: placement without value still validates (backwards compatible)
value random valid for all three families
valid id per family passes; bogus id fails with named error
wrong-family id (e.g. barrel=jester) fails

milestones.name: Composer Typed Spawn
milestones.objective: populateArea spawns one entity per placement using its declared value (random rolls from the family list); quota assignment logic is deleted.
milestones.success: Every placement in a macro produces exactly one spawned entity of the declared or rolled type; no budget under/over-placement remains possible.
milestones.diagram:
graph LR
  A[placement slot] --> B{value}
  B -->|random| C[rng.pick family list]
  B -->|specific id| D[use as-is]
  C --> E[spawn via factory]
  D --> E

tasks.name: Spawn from placeholder value
tasks.what: Rewrite populateArea in world/macros.js: every layout placement spawns directly; value 'random' rolls rng.pick over the family registry ids, specific values pass through. Delete chooseSlots/assignBarrelTypes/assignEnemyTypes/assignPowerupTypes quota logic. Keep solid-block guard and structure classification.
tasks.why: The placeholder becomes the single source of truth for what spawns; quotas are gone by design.
acceptance: specific value spawns that exact type
random always yields an id from the correct family list
same seed + same macros produce identical populations (determinism preserved)
budgets report shape retained (requested == placed == slot count)

tasks.name: Delete budget machinery
tasks.what: Remove stageBudgets generation (tension/stageMult/barrelMults blocks), hand-tuned per-stage barrels/enemies/powerups maps, getStageBudget and all its call sites (world/build.js, world/accessors.js if any) from world/levelConfigs.js. Update or delete the test assertions that exercise budgets (tuning.test.js, levelFlow.test.js, levelConfigs.test.js).
tasks.why: With typed placeholders the per-type quantity budget is obsolete; leaving it invites drift.
acceptance: grep for stageBudget/getStageBudget/barrelScale/barrelMults returns nothing in petal-panic/js
full test suite shows zero new failures vs baseline

milestones.name: Macro Migration
milestones.objective: All existing macro files get value: random on every barrel/enemy/powerup placement — clean data, no fallbacks in code.
milestones.success: Every placement in petal-panic/macros carries an explicit value; all macros still pass schema validation.
milestones.diagram:
graph LR
  A[18 macro files] --> B[script adds value=random to 100 placements]
  B --> C[schema validate all macros]
  C --> D[green]

tasks.name: Migrate macros to random
tasks.what: Write and run a one-off script that walks petal-panic/macros/**/*.json and sets value: 'random' on every placement whose type is barrel/enemy/powerup (none have value today). Then validate every migrated macro against the schema.
tasks.why: Existing levels must keep working under the new composer; defaulting them to random preserves current behavior with zero code fallbacks.
acceptance: all 100 placements across 18 level files carry value random
every macro file passes assertMacroSchema after migration
verify: python3 -c "import json,glob; ps=[p for f in glob.glob('petal-panic/macros/levels/*.json') for p in json.load(open(f)).get('placements',[])]; print(len([p for p in ps if p.get('value')=='random']))"

milestones.name: Macro Editor UX
milestones.objective: The editor lets the user pick a concrete type per placeholder by clicking, cycling random through the family list dynamically; hovering shows the current value.
milestones.success: Clicking a placement dot cycles random to first type to last type back to random; tooltip reads e.g. 'barrel - coin'; lists come from the registries so new types appear automatically.
milestones.diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
  random --> wood : click
  wood --> explosive : click
  explosive --> coin : click
  coin --> random : click

tasks.name: Editor value cycle and tooltip
tasks.what: In macro-editor (js/pointer.js + js/state.js + js/draw.js or wherever placement dots are handled): clicking a barrel/enemy/powerup placement cycles its value random to each id in the family registry order back to random; hovering the dot shows a tooltip like 'barrel - random' using the registry label. Import the three registries from the game JS so the cycle is dynamic.
tasks.why: The user must be able to pin specific types without hardcoding anything in the editor; labels come from object meta.
acceptance: clicking cycles random to all family ids back to random in registry order
hovering the dot shows 'family - label' (e.g. 'barrel - Coin')
saved macro persists the chosen value and reloads it
verify: manual: open macro editor, click a barrel dot through full cycle, save, reload, verify persisted value

milestones.name: Verification
milestones.objective: Prove the whole typed-spawn flow end to end and that nothing regressed.
milestones.success: Unit tests cover schema + composer behavior; full suite at baseline or better; a manual playthrough spawns the declared types.
milestones.diagram:
graph LR
  A[unit tests] --> C[full suite]
  B[manual editor cycle] --> C
  C --> D[play level - spawned types match placeholders]

tasks.name: Typed spawn test coverage
tasks.what: Add unit tests: schema accepts/rejects value per family; composer spawns exact type for specific values; random draws stay within the family list; determinism (same seed same population); migrated macros validate. Run the full suite and compare against the pre-change baseline failure set.
tasks.why: The quota removal touches level building broadly; the regression gate must be explicit, not vibes.
acceptance: specific value spawns that exact type (all three families)
random never yields an id outside the family list (statistical: N rolls all valid)
same seed + macros yields identical population twice
full node --test run shows zero new failures vs baseline
